citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the selected pure four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang–Mills model with global gauge group $SU(2)$ and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets. Let $U$ be a simply connected regular patch of its source-proposed Seiberg–Witten Coulomb branch on which the local periods $a,a_D:U\to\mathbb C$ are holomorphic and $\operatorname{Im}(\partial a_D/\partial a)>0$. The earlier Coulomb-branch data define the formal charge-label lattice $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with labels $\gamma=(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing $\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The source-proposed model convention fixes the scalar central charge to be $z_u(\gamma)=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)$; $a,a_D,z_u$ have mass dimension one, $u$ has mass dimension two, and charge labels and pairings are dimensionless.

For the model-specific physical charge data used here, equip $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ with the integral antisymmetric Dirac pairing

$$\langle(n_e,n_m),(n'_e,n'_m)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2(n_m n'_e-n_e n'_m).$$

In particular the source-designated monopole label $\gamma_m=(0,1)$ and dyon label $\gamma_d=(1,-1)$ satisfy $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2$, the convention matched by a two-arrow Kronecker quiver with both arrows directed from the dyon vertex to the monopole vertex. The lattice records formal charge labels only: it does not assert that every label is an allowed line operator or a realized particle.

For each $u\in U$, the selected model supplies a stable support $\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$. For each $\gamma\in\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$, supply an abstract one-particle massive rest-fiber Hilbert sector $\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ with positive inner product linear in its first variable, a bounded self-adjoint grading involution, a positive rest mass $M_{u,\gamma}$, and the conserved label $\gamma$. On a supplied common dense graded invariant domain $\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$, supply the $\mathcal N=2$ supertranslation representation of the earlier BPS-state definition: $P^0=M_{u,\gamma}I$, $P^j=0$, $Z^{12}=z_u(\gamma)I$, $Z^{21}=-z_u(\gamma)I$, and closed odd supercharges $Q^I_\alpha$ with their actual Hilbert adjoints, with every product in the bracket table defined there. Use metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, so $P_0=-M_{u,\gamma}I$. This fiber is not asserted to be a normalizable fixed-momentum subspace of a full super-Poincaré Hilbert representation.

The spin-cover Lorentz action on vectors is characterized by $\Phi(\Lambda_gx)=g\Phi(x)g^\dagger$ for $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$ and $\Phi(x)=-\sigma^\mu x_\mu$, as in the unitary representation definition. For the rest vector $P_{u,\gamma}=(M_{u,\gamma},0,0,0)$ define its stabilizer
$$G_{P_{u,\gamma}}:=\{g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C):\Lambda_gP_{u,\gamma}=P_{u,\gamma}\}=\mathrm{SU}(2).$$
Indeed $\Phi(P_{u,\gamma})=M_{u,\gamma}I_2$, so the stabilizer condition is $gg^\dagger=I_2$. Separately supply a grading-preserving unitary representation $\pi_{u,\gamma}:\mathrm{SU}(2)\to\mathcal U(\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma})$, meaning $\pi(gh)=\pi(g)\pi(h)$, $\pi(I)=I$, and $\pi(g)^*\pi(g)=I=\pi(g)\pi(g)^*$. Require strong continuity: $g\mapsto\pi(g)\psi$ is norm-continuous for every $\psi$. Require $\pi(g)\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}=\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$ and, on that domain,
$$\pi(g)Q^I_\alpha\pi(g)^{-1}=\sum_\beta g^\beta{}_{\alpha}Q^I_\beta,\qquad \pi(g)(Q^I_\alpha)^*\pi(g)^{-1}=\sum_\beta\overline{g^\beta{}_{\alpha}}(Q^I_\beta)^*,$$
where $g^\beta{}_{\alpha}$ is row $\beta$, column $\alpha$; scalar momenta and central charges are unchanged. This is supplied rest-fiber rotation data, not a restriction of an unspecified full-space operator $U(g,0)$. Choose the spin axis $3$ and the one-parameter rotation subgroup
$$r_3(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\theta/2}&0\\0&e^{i\theta/2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z).$$
Supply a nonzero closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ invariant under this supplied $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ action and identified as the selected BPS sector. Its vectors lie in $\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$, and every nonzero vector is BPS-saturated in the exact sense of the earlier BPS-state definition: $M_{u,\gamma}=|z_u(\gamma)|$, and the two $\mathcal N=2$ annihilating supercharge combinations in that definition vanish on them. Stability is supplied model data: this sector is discrete and separated by a positive spectral gap from the multiparticle continuum at the same conserved charge. The sector and gap are inputs, not conclusions here. On $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$, supply a self-adjoint operator $J_3$ with $2J_3$-integer spectrum such that the restricted action of $r_3(\theta)$ is $e^{-i\theta J_3}$ for every $\theta\in\mathbb R$. Require its spectral calculus to define a bounded trace-class operator $B_{u,\gamma}=(-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2$, and supply a Hilbert basis $E_{u,\gamma}$ of $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$.

Define the four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ second-helicity supertrace, also called the $B_2$ index here, by

$$\Omega_u(\gamma)=-\frac12\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}(B_{u,\gamma}),$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}$ is the absolutely convergent supplied-basis trace of a trace-class operator; basis independence is not needed here. Set $\Omega_u(\gamma)=0$ for $\gamma\notin\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$. The trace convention uses only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the stated mathematical suppliers, not full Choice. No existence or local constancy of this support is asserted.

Let $\mathcal C\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$ be any chosen set of charges, and fix $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. At each $u\in U$ for which $e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ for every $\gamma\in\mathcal C$, define $\phi_u(\gamma)=\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma))/\pi\in(0,1)$ for $\gamma\in\mathcal C$. For two charges $\gamma,\delta$ with nonzero central charges, define their marginal-stability wall by

$$W_{\gamma,\delta}:=\{u\in U:z_u(\gamma)/z_u(\delta)\in\mathbb R_{>0}\}.$$

Given a specified family $\mathscr W$ of such wall subsets of $U$, a chamber relative to $\mathscr W$ is a connected component of $U\setminus\bigcup_{W\in\mathscr W}W$. A formal positive cone $\Gamma_+\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ used for ordered products contains $0$, is closed under addition, and is pointed ($\Gamma_+\cap(-\Gamma_+)=\{0\}$). It is supplied with an additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ that is positive on nonzero charges and has finite sublevel sets, meaning $\{\gamma\in\Gamma_+:\ell(\gamma)\le N\}$ is finite for every $N\in\mathbb N$. The definition is conditional on the existence of the Hilbert sectors, trace data, cone, and degree; it constructs no continuum theory and makes no Hall-index identification.

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite acyclic quiver, where $Q_0,Q_1$ are finite
sets and $s,t:Q_1\to Q_0$ are the source and target maps. Let $k=\mathbb F_q$
with $q>1$, and assign to each vertex $i\in Q_0$ a charge
$z_i\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$. A
finite-dimensional representation $M$ assigns a finite-dimensional
$k$-vector space $M_i$ to each vertex and a linear map
$M_a:M_{s(a)}\to M_{t(a)}$ to each arrow; its dimension vector is
$\mathbf d(M)=(\dim_k M_i)_{i\in Q_0}$. Put
$Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i z_i$ and, for nonzero
$\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$, put
$\phi_Z(\mathbf d)=\arg Z(\mathbf d)/\pi$ using the principal argument. For
$M\ne0$, set $\phi_Z(M)=\phi_Z(\mathbf d(M))$. Call $M$
$Z$-semistable when every nonzero subrepresentation has phase at most
$\phi_Z(M)$. Include the zero representation as semistable with no assigned
phase.

Use the small finitary abelian skeleton of these representations. Its Hall
algebra has basis $\delta_M$ indexed by isomorphism classes, and the
subobject-first convention is
$(f\star g)(L)=\sum_{U\subseteq L}f(U)g(L/U)$, with distinct embedded
subobjects counted separately. Its dimension completion is the product of
the finite-dimensional homogeneous components. For integer dimension
vectors define the bilinear Euler form and its skew-symmetrization by
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d).$$

For a phase $\phi$, let
$$S_Z(\phi)=\delta_0+\sum_{\substack{[M]\ne[0]\\M\ Z\text{-semistable}\\\phi_Z(M)=\phi}}\delta_M,$$
where $\delta_M$ is the characteristic function of the isomorphism class
$[M]$ and $\delta_0$ is the Hall unit. The Euler and skew integrations are
the continuous maps
$$I(f)=\sum_{[M]}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}X^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad J(f)=\sum_{[M]}t^{\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(M))}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}x^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad t=\sqrt q>0,$$
as proved for this finite-field category by the Euler and skew integration
theorem. Their completed targets have bases $X^{\mathbf d}$ and
$x^{\mathbf d}$ and products
$$X^{\mathbf d}X^{\mathbf e}=q^{-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d)}X^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e},\qquad x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e}=t^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle}x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}.$$

Write $\Phi_Z=\{\phi_Z(\mathbf e):\mathbf e\in\mathbb N^{Q_0},\
\mathbf e\ne0\}$ and order its elements decreasingly. Define the Euler and
skew Hall spectrum generators by
$$P_Z^{E}:=\prod_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow} I(S_Z(\phi)),\qquad P_Z^{\mathrm{sk}}:=\mathop{*}_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow}J(S_Z(\phi)).$$
In each product the largest phase is the leftmost factor and multiplication
is in the corresponding completed torus. In any fixed total-dimension degree
$D$, only dimension vectors with $\sum_i d_i\le D$ and their finitely many
phases can contribute. Thus these are degreewise formal products in the
specified completion; no analytic convergence is asserted.

These generators describe the Euler or skew integration of finite-field
semistable representation groupoids. Calling such data protected BPS indices,
dimensions of physical state spaces, or spectra of a four-dimensional
supersymmetric model is an additional dictionary, not part of this
mathematical definition.

Let $Q$ be any finite acyclic quiver over $k=\mathbb F_q$, with no
finite-representation-type restriction, and let $Z_-$ and $Z_+$ assign a charge in
$\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ to every vertex. Use the
subobject-first dimension completion and the Euler and skew integrations
defined on this A page. Then
$$P_{Z_-}^E=P_{Z_+}^E,\qquad P_{Z_-}^{\mathrm{sk}}=P_{Z_+}^{\mathrm{sk}}.$$
Each is a unit with constant term $1$ in its own completed quantum torus.
Consequently conjugation by the two generators defines the same continuous
automorphism on each corresponding completed torus. The products and
automorphisms are formal in the dimension completion. This is a finite-field
Hall identity only; it makes no physical state-counting identification.

derivations.claim: For a supported charge $\gamma\in\Sigma_u$, put $n_\delta=\Omega_u(\gamma)\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}\in\mathbb Z$. Since $\ell(\gamma)>0$, the binomial expansion of $1-\varepsilon(\gamma)y^\gamma$ to any integer power is defined degreewise in the stated completion: terms of order $k$ have degree increased by $k\ell(\gamma)$. Bilinearity gives $n_{\delta+\delta'}=n_\delta+n_{\delta'}$, so the formula for $\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}$ is multiplicative on monomials and hence on series by continuity. It fixes $y^\gamma$ because the pairing is alternating, and replacing $n_\delta$ by $-n_\delta$ gives its inverse. Every correction term raises degree, so $\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}$ and its inverse preserve each $F^N$ and define elements of $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{fil}}(\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}})$. Finite sublevels of $\Gamma_+$ and finiteness of the support in each degree sublevel ensure each bounded-degree truncation of the ordered composition uses only finitely many input terms and factors. Thus the phase-ordered composition $\mathcal S_u$ is defined in the inverse-limit topology.

The formula for $\Phi$ preserves products on basis monomials: $\Phi(x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e})=\sigma(t)^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle_Q}Y^{\rho(\mathbf d+\mathbf e)}$, while $\Phi(x^{\mathbf d})\star_v\Phi(x^{\mathbf e})=v^{-\langle\rho(\mathbf e),\rho(\mathbf d)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}Y^{\rho(\mathbf d+\mathbf e)}$. The pairing identity and $\sigma(t)=v$ make these expressions equal. The Statement requires $\ell(\rho(\mathbf d))=\sum_i d_i$ for every $\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$; this degree identity makes $\Phi$ continuous on the total-dimension and $\ell$-degree completions.

The finite-field hypotheses of [F3] hold for the same $Q$ and the two assignments $Z_{u_-},Z_{u_+}$, since their vertex values lie in $\mathbb H$ by the common phase rotation. Therefore $P_{Z_{u_-}}^{\mathrm{sk}}=P_{Z_{u_+}}^{\mathrm{sk}}$ as units of the completed Hall skew torus.

Apply the continuous homomorphism $\Phi$ from step 1.2 to the degreewise equality in step 1.3. Equal coefficients remain equal under the coefficient embedding and charge map, so $\Phi(P_{Z_{u_-}}^{\mathrm{sk}})=\Phi(P_{Z_{u_+}}^{\mathrm{sk}})$.

Since $\Theta$ is continuous for the stated unit-group and inverse-limit automorphism topologies, applying it to step 2.1 preserves equality. The Hall generator is the decreasing-phase product of the factors $J(S_{Z_u}(\phi))$; multiplicativity of $\Phi$ and $\Theta$ and the per-phase identity in [A2] therefore identify each image with the corresponding physical phase factor, in the same order. Degreewise continuity and finite degree sublevels in [A3] pass this equality from finite truncations to the full products. The phase condition on $\Sigma_u$ ensures every factor used in that bridge is defined, and $\Sigma_u\subseteq\Gamma_+\setminus\{0\}$ excludes the undefined zero-charge phase. [F1] supplies the second-helicity index convention, and [A1] records its choice-strength premise. Thus $\mathcal S_{u_-}=\mathcal S_{u_+}$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver: $Q_0$ and $Q_1$ are finite sets,
and $s,t:Q_1\to Q_0$ give the source and target of each arrow. Assume $Q$ has
no directed cycles. For a field $K$, a finite-dimensional representation $M$
assigns a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $M_i$ to each $i\in Q_0$ and a
linear map $M_a:M_{s(a)}\to M_{t(a)}$ to each $a\in Q_1$. A morphism is a
family of linear maps at the vertices commuting with all arrow maps. Write
$\mathcal A_Q(K)$ for this category and
$\mathbf d(M)=(\dim_K M_i)_{i\in Q_0}\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ for its dimension
vector. For the finite-field Hall branch, fix $k=\mathbb F_q$ and write
$\mathcal A_Q=\mathcal A_Q(k)$. The next lemma proves the abelian and Euler
properties over any field; over $k$ it constructs a small finitary abelian
skeleton of $\mathcal A_Q$, so $\mathcal A_Q$ is essentially small.

For $\mathbf d,\mathbf e\in\mathbb Z^{Q_0}$ define the bilinear form
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,$$
and its skew-symmetrization
$\langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d)$.
The next lemma proves that $\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(N))$ is the
Hom-minus-Yoneda-Ext$^1$ dimension for this arrow convention.

Fix $z_i\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ for each
vertex and extend $Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i z_i$ additively. If
$\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ is nonzero, then
$\operatorname{Im}Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i\operatorname{Im}z_i>0$; thus its
principal argument lies in $(0,\pi)$. For a nonzero representation $M$, put
$\phi_Z(M)=\arg Z(\mathbf d(M))/\pi\in(0,1)$. Call
$M$ **$Z$-semistable** if every nonzero subrepresentation $U\subseteq M$
satisfies $\phi_Z(U)\le\phi_Z(M)$, and **$Z$-stable** if the inequality is
strict for every proper nonzero subrepresentation.

For the semistable groupoids and stacks below, include the zero representation
as semistable without assigning it a phase. Stable objects and HN factors
remain nonzero.

For a dimension vector $\mathbf d$, let
$$\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}(Q)=\prod_{a:i\to j} \operatorname{Hom}_k(k^{d_i},k^{d_j}),\qquad G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}_{d_i,k}.$$
The group $G_{\mathbf d}$ acts by change of bases. Define
$\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf d}(Q,Z)$ geometrically: its points over an
algebraic closure $\bar k$ are representations for which every nonzero
$\bar k$-subrepresentation satisfies the semistability inequality. The
associated quotient stack is
$\mathfrak M^{ss}_{\mathbf d}(Q,Z)=[\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf d}(Q,Z)/G_{\mathbf d}]$.
For $\mathbf d=0$, set $\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf0}=\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf0}=\operatorname{Spec}k$.
The group $G_{\mathbf0}$ is trivial, so its rational-point groupoid has one
zero object, trivial automorphism group, and cardinality $1$.
Here $[X/G]$ denotes the groupoid-valued quotient: over a scheme $S$ its
objects are $G$-torsors on $S$ with equivariant maps to $X$, and its arrows
are equivariant isomorphisms over $S$. The openness lemma below proves that
$\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf d}$ is open.

For a finite groupoid $\mathcal G$, define its groupoid cardinality by
$$|\mathcal G|=\sum_{[x]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal G)} \frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal G}(x)|}.$$
The rational-point groupoid of $\mathfrak M^{ss}_{\mathbf d}$ is finite, and
the finite-field descent lemma identifies it with the groupoid of finite-field
semistable representations and their isomorphisms. No Calabi–Yau structure,
potential, orientation data, vanishing cycles, or physical state-counting
identification is part of this definition.

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite acyclic quiver, where $Q_0,Q_1$ are finite
sets and $s,t:Q_1\to Q_0$ are the source and target maps. Let $k=\mathbb F_q$
with $q>1$, and assign to each vertex $i\in Q_0$ a charge
$z_i\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$. A
finite-dimensional representation $M$ assigns a finite-dimensional
$k$-vector space $M_i$ to each vertex and a linear map
$M_a:M_{s(a)}\to M_{t(a)}$ to each arrow; its dimension vector is
$\mathbf d(M)=(\dim_k M_i)_{i\in Q_0}$. Put
$Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i z_i$ and, for nonzero
$\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$, put
$\phi_Z(\mathbf d)=\arg Z(\mathbf d)/\pi$ using the principal argument. For
$M\ne0$, set $\phi_Z(M)=\phi_Z(\mathbf d(M))$. Call $M$
$Z$-semistable when every nonzero subrepresentation has phase at most
$\phi_Z(M)$. Include the zero representation as semistable with no assigned
phase.

Use the small finitary abelian skeleton of these representations. Its Hall
algebra has basis $\delta_M$ indexed by isomorphism classes, and the
subobject-first convention is
$(f\star g)(L)=\sum_{U\subseteq L}f(U)g(L/U)$, with distinct embedded
subobjects counted separately. Its dimension completion is the product of
the finite-dimensional homogeneous components. For integer dimension
vectors define the bilinear Euler form and its skew-symmetrization by
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d).$$

For a phase $\phi$, let
$$S_Z(\phi)=\delta_0+\sum_{\substack{[M]\ne[0]\\M\ Z\text{-semistable}\\\phi_Z(M)=\phi}}\delta_M,$$
where $\delta_M$ is the characteristic function of the isomorphism class
$[M]$ and $\delta_0$ is the Hall unit. The Euler and skew integrations are
the continuous maps
$$I(f)=\sum_{[M]}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}X^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad J(f)=\sum_{[M]}t^{\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(M))}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}x^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad t=\sqrt q>0,$$
as proved for this finite-field category by the Euler and skew integration
theorem. Their completed targets have bases $X^{\mathbf d}$ and
$x^{\mathbf d}$ and products
$$X^{\mathbf d}X^{\mathbf e}=q^{-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d)}X^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e},\qquad x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e}=t^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle}x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}.$$

Write $\Phi_Z=\{\phi_Z(\mathbf e):\mathbf e\in\mathbb N^{Q_0},\
\mathbf e\ne0\}$ and order its elements decreasingly. Define the Euler and
skew Hall spectrum generators by
$$P_Z^{E}:=\prod_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow} I(S_Z(\phi)),\qquad P_Z^{\mathrm{sk}}:=\mathop{*}_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow}J(S_Z(\phi)).$$
In each product the largest phase is the leftmost factor and multiplication
is in the corresponding completed torus. In any fixed total-dimension degree
$D$, only dimension vectors with $\sum_i d_i\le D$ and their finitely many
phases can contribute. Thus these are degreewise formal products in the
specified completion; no analytic convergence is asserted.

These generators describe the Euler or skew integration of finite-field
semistable representation groupoids. Calling such data protected BPS indices,
dimensions of physical state spaces, or spectra of a four-dimensional
supersymmetric model is an additional dictionary, not part of this
mathematical definition.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the selected pure four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang–Mills model with global gauge group $SU(2)$ and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets. Let $U$ be a simply connected regular patch of its source-proposed Seiberg–Witten Coulomb branch on which the local periods $a,a_D:U\to\mathbb C$ are holomorphic and $\operatorname{Im}(\partial a_D/\partial a)>0$. The earlier Coulomb-branch data define the formal charge-label lattice $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with labels $\gamma=(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing $\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The source-proposed model convention fixes the scalar central charge to be $z_u(\gamma)=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)$; $a,a_D,z_u$ have mass dimension one, $u$ has mass dimension two, and charge labels and pairings are dimensionless.

For the model-specific physical charge data used here, equip $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ with the integral antisymmetric Dirac pairing

$$\langle(n_e,n_m),(n'_e,n'_m)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2(n_m n'_e-n_e n'_m).$$

In particular the source-designated monopole label $\gamma_m=(0,1)$ and dyon label $\gamma_d=(1,-1)$ satisfy $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2$, the convention matched by a two-arrow Kronecker quiver with both arrows directed from the dyon vertex to the monopole vertex. The lattice records formal charge labels only: it does not assert that every label is an allowed line operator or a realized particle.

For each $u\in U$, the selected model supplies a stable support $\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$. For each $\gamma\in\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$, supply an abstract one-particle massive rest-fiber Hilbert sector $\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ with positive inner product linear in its first variable, a bounded self-adjoint grading involution, a positive rest mass $M_{u,\gamma}$, and the conserved label $\gamma$. On a supplied common dense graded invariant domain $\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$, supply the $\mathcal N=2$ supertranslation representation of the earlier BPS-state definition: $P^0=M_{u,\gamma}I$, $P^j=0$, $Z^{12}=z_u(\gamma)I$, $Z^{21}=-z_u(\gamma)I$, and closed odd supercharges $Q^I_\alpha$ with their actual Hilbert adjoints, with every product in the bracket table defined there. Use metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, so $P_0=-M_{u,\gamma}I$. This fiber is not asserted to be a normalizable fixed-momentum subspace of a full super-Poincaré Hilbert representation.

The spin-cover Lorentz action on vectors is characterized by $\Phi(\Lambda_gx)=g\Phi(x)g^\dagger$ for $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$ and $\Phi(x)=-\sigma^\mu x_\mu$, as in the unitary representation definition. For the rest vector $P_{u,\gamma}=(M_{u,\gamma},0,0,0)$ define its stabilizer
$$G_{P_{u,\gamma}}:=\{g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C):\Lambda_gP_{u,\gamma}=P_{u,\gamma}\}=\mathrm{SU}(2).$$
Indeed $\Phi(P_{u,\gamma})=M_{u,\gamma}I_2$, so the stabilizer condition is $gg^\dagger=I_2$. Separately supply a grading-preserving unitary representation $\pi_{u,\gamma}:\mathrm{SU}(2)\to\mathcal U(\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma})$, meaning $\pi(gh)=\pi(g)\pi(h)$, $\pi(I)=I$, and $\pi(g)^*\pi(g)=I=\pi(g)\pi(g)^*$. Require strong continuity: $g\mapsto\pi(g)\psi$ is norm-continuous for every $\psi$. Require $\pi(g)\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}=\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$ and, on that domain,
$$\pi(g)Q^I_\alpha\pi(g)^{-1}=\sum_\beta g^\beta{}_{\alpha}Q^I_\beta,\qquad \pi(g)(Q^I_\alpha)^*\pi(g)^{-1}=\sum_\beta\overline{g^\beta{}_{\alpha}}(Q^I_\beta)^*,$$
where $g^\beta{}_{\alpha}$ is row $\beta$, column $\alpha$; scalar momenta and central charges are unchanged. This is supplied rest-fiber rotation data, not a restriction of an unspecified full-space operator $U(g,0)$. Choose the spin axis $3$ and the one-parameter rotation subgroup
$$r_3(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\theta/2}&0\\0&e^{i\theta/2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z).$$
Supply a nonzero closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ invariant under this supplied $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ action and identified as the selected BPS sector. Its vectors lie in $\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$, and every nonzero vector is BPS-saturated in the exact sense of the earlier BPS-state definition: $M_{u,\gamma}=|z_u(\gamma)|$, and the two $\mathcal N=2$ annihilating supercharge combinations in that definition vanish on them. Stability is supplied model data: this sector is discrete and separated by a positive spectral gap from the multiparticle continuum at the same conserved charge. The sector and gap are inputs, not conclusions here. On $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$, supply a self-adjoint operator $J_3$ with $2J_3$-integer spectrum such that the restricted action of $r_3(\theta)$ is $e^{-i\theta J_3}$ for every $\theta\in\mathbb R$. Require its spectral calculus to define a bounded trace-class operator $B_{u,\gamma}=(-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2$, and supply a Hilbert basis $E_{u,\gamma}$ of $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$.

Define the four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ second-helicity supertrace, also called the $B_2$ index here, by

$$\Omega_u(\gamma)=-\frac12\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}(B_{u,\gamma}),$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}$ is the absolutely convergent supplied-basis trace of a trace-class operator; basis independence is not needed here. Set $\Omega_u(\gamma)=0$ for $\gamma\notin\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$. The trace convention uses only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the stated mathematical suppliers, not full Choice. No existence or local constancy of this support is asserted.

Let $\mathcal C\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$ be any chosen set of charges, and fix $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. At each $u\in U$ for which $e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ for every $\gamma\in\mathcal C$, define $\phi_u(\gamma)=\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma))/\pi\in(0,1)$ for $\gamma\in\mathcal C$. For two charges $\gamma,\delta$ with nonzero central charges, define their marginal-stability wall by

$$W_{\gamma,\delta}:=\{u\in U:z_u(\gamma)/z_u(\delta)\in\mathbb R_{>0}\}.$$

Given a specified family $\mathscr W$ of such wall subsets of $U$, a chamber relative to $\mathscr W$ is a connected component of $U\setminus\bigcup_{W\in\mathscr W}W$. A formal positive cone $\Gamma_+\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ used for ordered products contains $0$, is closed under addition, and is pointed ($\Gamma_+\cap(-\Gamma_+)=\{0\}$). It is supplied with an additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ that is positive on nonzero charges and has finite sublevel sets, meaning $\{\gamma\in\Gamma_+:\ell(\gamma)\le N\}$ is finite for every $N\in\mathbb N$. The definition is conditional on the existence of the Hilbert sectors, trace data, cone, and degree; it constructs no continuum theory and makes no Hall-index identification.

Let $\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ and define
$\phi(z)=\arg(z)/\pi\in(0,1)$. For $z,w\in\mathbb H$, the phase of $z+w$
lies between $\phi(z)$ and $\phi(w)$, strictly between them when they are
unequal and equal to their common value when they coincide.

Let $Q$ be any finite acyclic quiver over $k=\mathbb F_q$, with no
finite-representation-type restriction, and let $Z_-$ and $Z_+$ assign a charge in
$\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ to every vertex. Use the
subobject-first dimension completion and the Euler and skew integrations
defined on this A page. Then
$$P_{Z_-}^E=P_{Z_+}^E,\qquad P_{Z_-}^{\mathrm{sk}}=P_{Z_+}^{\mathrm{sk}}.$$
Each is a unit with constant term $1$ in its own completed quantum torus.
Consequently conjugation by the two generators defines the same continuous
automorphism on each corresponding completed torus. The products and
automorphisms are formal in the dimension completion. This is a finite-field
Hall identity only; it makes no physical state-counting identification.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the supplied trace-class BPS-index data. Use the selected pure four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang–Mills model with global gauge group $SU(2)$ and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets, in natural units $c=\hbar=1$. On a simply connected regular patch $U$, the local periods $a,a_D:U\to\mathbb C$ are holomorphic and satisfy $\operatorname{Im}(\partial a_D/\partial a)>0$. Its formal charge-label lattice is $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with
$$z_u(n_e,n_m)=\sqrt2\bigl(n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)\bigr),\qquad \langle(n_e,n_m),(n'_e,n'_m)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2(n_mn'_e-n_en'_m).$$
For each supplied stable one-particle BPS rest sector, $\Omega_u(\gamma)$ is the second-helicity trace $-\frac12\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}\!\bigl((-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2\bigr)$ from the physical charge-data definition; it is set to zero off the selected stable support. Let $u_-,u_+\in U$ be two specified points.

The finite-field Hall input is a finite acyclic quiver $Q$ over $\mathbb F_q$, where $q>1$ is a prime power. For integer dimension vectors, define
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d),\qquad t=\sqrt q>0.$$

Suppose an additive map $\rho:\mathbb Z^{Q_0}\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and a physical charge cone $\Gamma_+$ are supplied, where $\Gamma_+$ contains $0$, is closed under addition and is pointed, such that $\rho(\mathbb N^{Q_0})\subseteq\Gamma_+$. Supply a positive additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ with finite sublevel sets and require $\ell(\rho(\mathbf d))=\sum_i d_i$ for every $\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$. Assume also, for all $\mathbf d,\mathbf e\in\mathbb Z^{Q_0}$, that

$$\langle\rho(\mathbf d),\rho(\mathbf e)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=\langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q.$$

Let $\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$. Choose one real phase rotation $\alpha$ such that for both $u\in\{u_-,u_+\}$ the vertex charges $Z_u(\mathbf e_i)=e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf e_i))$ lie in $\mathbb H$, and extend each assignment additively by $Z_u(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i Z_u(\mathbf e_i)=e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf d))$. 
A representation $M$ assigns a finite-dimensional $\mathbb F_q$-vector space to each vertex and a linear map to each arrow; its dimension vector is $\mathbf d(M)\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$. The additive central charge $Z_u(\mathbf d)$ was specified above. For nonzero $\mathbf d$, set $\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d)=\arg Z_u(\mathbf d)/\pi\in(0,1)$; this range follows because a nonzero sum of upper-half-plane vertex charges lies in $\mathbb H$. For every nonzero dimension vector, the defining equality for $Z_u$ identifies $\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d)$ with $\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf d)))/\pi$. A nonzero $M$ is $Z_u$-semistable when every nonzero subrepresentation $U\subseteq M$ satisfies $\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d(U))\le\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d(M))$.

On the isomorphism-class basis $\delta_M$, the subobject-first Hall product is $(f\star g)(L)=\sum_{U\subseteq L}f(U)g(L/U)$, with distinct embedded subobjects counted separately. Complete by total dimension, that is, take the product over dimension vectors of the finite-dimensional homogeneous components. For a phase $\phi$, put $S_{Z_u}(\phi)=\delta_0+\sum_{[M]\ne[0],\,M\ Z_u\text{-semistable},\,\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d(M))=\phi}\delta_M$, where $\delta_0$ is the Hall unit. Its skew integration is $J(f)=\sum_{[M]}t^{\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(M))}f(M)|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|^{-1}x^{\mathbf d(M)}$, and the completed skew torus has product $x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e}=t^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle_Q}x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}$. The resulting Hall spectrum generator is the decreasing-phase product $P_{Z_u}^{\mathrm{sk}}=\mathop{*}_{\phi}^{\searrow}J(S_{Z_u}(\phi))$, with the largest phase leftmost.

For each of the two specified points define the nonzero index support
$$\Sigma_u:=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_+\setminus\{0\}:\Omega_u(\gamma)\ne0\}.$$
Assume $\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}:\Omega_u(\gamma)\ne0\}\subseteq\Gamma_+$ for both specified points, so $\Sigma_u$ is the full nonzero index support. Assume $\{\gamma\in\Sigma_u:\ell(\gamma)\le N\}$ is finite for every $N\ge0$, $\Omega_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb Z$ on $\Sigma_u$, and $e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb H$ for every $u\in\{u_-,u_+\}$ and $\gamma\in\Sigma_u$. Thus every phase $\phi_u(\gamma)=\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma))/\pi$ used below is defined. Zero charge is excluded from $\Sigma_u$ and from all phase-indexed products.

Let $K_{\mathrm{phys}}$ be a coefficient field with a field embedding $\sigma:\mathbb Q(t)\to K_{\mathrm{phys}}$, and write $v:=\sigma(t)$ for the dimensionless Hall coefficient parameter. Here $\mathbb Q(t)=\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)$ is the field generated by the specified algebraic number $t$, so $v^2=q$ and $v\ne1$; $v$ is distinct from the physical constant $\hbar=1$ fixed by natural units. Use the supplied additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ with $\ell(0)=0$, $\ell(\gamma)>0$ for $\gamma\ne0$, and finite sublevel sets. Define the commutative formal charge-series algebra and the quantum charge torus by

$$\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}:=\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma_+}K_{\mathrm{phys}}y^\gamma,\qquad y^\gamma y^\delta=y^{\gamma+\delta},$$

$$\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}:=\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma_+}K_{\mathrm{phys}}Y^\gamma,\qquad Y^\gamma\star_v Y^\delta=v^{-\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}Y^{\gamma+\delta}.$$

For either algebra and $N\ge0$, let $F^N$ consist of series supported on charges $\gamma$ with $\ell(\gamma)\ge N$. Give both algebras the linear topology whose neighborhoods of zero are the $F^N$. Finite sublevel sets make every truncation modulo $F^N$ finite-dimensional; the algebras are separated and complete, and their products are degreewise finite. Give $\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}^\times$ the subspace topology from $\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}$. For each $N\ge1$, let $G_N$ be the group of $K_{\mathrm{phys}}$-algebra automorphisms of $\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}/F^N$ preserving every induced quotient filtration subspace $F^j/F^N$ for $1\le j<N$, with reduction as the transition maps and the discrete topology on each $G_N$. Define $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{fil}}(\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}):=\varprojlim_{N\ge1}G_N$ with the inverse-limit topology. It is the group of continuous automorphisms and continuous inverses preserving the degree filtration.

The charge map and coefficient embedding define the degree-continuous torus map, extended from the total-dimension-completed Hall skew torus by continuity,

$$\Phi(x^{\mathbf d})=Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)},\qquad \Phi(c x^{\mathbf d})=\sigma(c)Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)}.$$

The degree identity $\ell(\rho(\mathbf d))=\sum_i d_i$ for $\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ ensures this continuity. On the commutative completed charge series, supply a sign refinement $\varepsilon:\Gamma_+\to\{\pm1\}$ with $\varepsilon(0)=1$ and $\varepsilon(\gamma+\delta)=(-1)^{\langle\gamma,\delta\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}\varepsilon(\gamma)\varepsilon(\delta)$. Define the physical KS factor for each $\gamma\in\Sigma_u$ by

$$\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}(y^\delta)=y^\delta\bigl(1-\varepsilon(\gamma)y^\gamma\bigr)^{\Omega_u(\gamma)\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}.$$

The integer power is interpreted by its formal binomial series in the degree topology. When charges have equal phase, order their labels lexicographically as integer pairs $(n_e,n_m)$. Let $\mathcal S_u$ be the composition of these factors over $\Sigma_u$ in decreasing phase order, with the largest phase leftmost and the stated lexicographic order within each phase. Finally assume an exact model-specific bridge: there is a continuous group homomorphism
$$\Theta:\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}^\times\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{fil}}(\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}),$$
and for every phase $\phi$ and either specified point it satisfies, using the same within-phase order,
$$\Theta\!\left(\Phi(J(S_{Z_u}(\phi)))\right)=\prod_{\substack{\gamma\in\Sigma_u\\\phi_u(\gamma)=\phi}}^{\searrow}\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}.$$

Here $S_{Z_u}(\phi)$ and $J$ are the semistable phase factor and skew integration from the finite-field Hall definition. Then

$$\mathcal S_{u_-}=\mathcal S_{u_+}.$$

This is a conditional transport theorem. The specified per-phase bridge is an additional physical input; neither the finite-field Hall identity nor this theorem asserts that the pure-SU(2) model supplies it, that the resulting index counts exist, or that the model has a continuum quantum-field-theory construction.

derivations.claim: In dimension $(1,1)$ each vertex space is $\mathbb F_q$. The two arrow maps are a pair $(r,s)\in\mathbb F_q^2$, and a change of bases $(g_m,g_d)\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^2$ sends $(r,s)$ to $(g_m r g_d^{-1},g_m s g_d^{-1})$. Hence the zero pair is one orbit and the nonzero pairs are classified by their one-dimensional spans in $\mathbb F_q^2$, giving $|\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)|=(q^2-1)/(q-1)=q+1$ nonzero isomorphism classes.

For a nonzero pair, an automorphism must satisfy $g_m r=r g_d$ and $g_m s=s g_d$; at least one arrow scalar is nonzero, so $g_m=g_d$ and the automorphism group has order $q-1$. For the zero pair every pair of base changes is allowed, so its automorphism group has order $(q-1)^2$.

The subrepresentation supported only at $m$ exists for every representation because both arrows have source $d$. The subrepresentation supported only at $d$ exists exactly for the zero pair. At $u_-$, where $\phi_m<\phi_d$, [F4] places the total phase between the two vertex phases; thus every nonzero pair has only the lower-phase proper subrepresentation at $m$ and is stable, whereas the zero pair has the higher-phase subrepresentation at $d$ and is unstable. At $u_+$, where $\phi_d<\phi_m$, the subrepresentation at $m$ has higher phase than the total for every pair, so none is semistable.

At $u_-$, the stable groupoid cardinality is the sum of $q+1$ weights $1/(q-1)$, namely $(q+1)/(q-1)$. For $\mathbf d=(1,1)$ and two arrows $d\to m$, $\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf d)=1+1-2=0$, so the skew integration contributes the factor $t^0=1$ and leaves this exact coefficient.

The charge map preserves the skew form on the basis pair: the two-arrow orientation gives $\langle\mathbf e_m,\mathbf e_d\rangle_Q=2$, equal to $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}$ by [F3]. Applying [F5] to the two phase assignments proves equality of the full completed Hall generators. If the bridge in [F6] is supplied with these exact phases and pairings, the physical KS products agree by the conditional theorem. The coefficient $(q+1)/(q-1)$ remains the finite-field groupoid weight computed in step 3.1; no step identifies it with the physical index $\Omega_u(\gamma_m+\gamma_d)$.
